claims.claim: The Frameworks repository is public and actively maintained.
claims.method: GitHub API: created 2024-05-31, last push 2026-11-27, 99 stars, 83 forks. Releases v0.0.1 (2026-09-01), v0.0.2 (2026-10-13), v0.0.3 (2026-11-11). 308 commits since 2025-12-01 (commits API page count).

claims.claim: Frameworks has 30+ sections shaped by dozens of contributors.
claims.method: The docs/pages folder holds about 34 topic folders. The GitHub contributors API returned 49 contributors. Quality of sections was not assessed.

claims.claim: Content is published under CC BY-SA 4.0.
claims.method: The LICENSE file reads Security Frameworks (c) 2026 by Security Alliance, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION because it is not a code license.
llms.txt (about 14 KB) and llms-full.txt (about 2.4 MB) return HTTP 200 with framework content. A frameworks-mcp repository exists and was last pushed 2026-05-15. Export accuracy was not checked.

claims.claim: Frontend and most infrastructure pages are unpublished drafts on the development site, not on the production site.
claims.method: The production navigation lists no Front-End/Web Application, Identity and Access Management, Encryption or Threat Modeling sections. The development site navigation lists them. This matches the proposal baseline as of 2026-11-28.

claims.claim: The proposal's three-area plan (AI security, infrastructure, frontend) will be completed within the grant.
claims.method: A future commitment. The funded pages could not yet be checked as complete.

claims.claim: SEAL is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by samczsun, with an operating runway of 8.5 months.
claims.method: The site footer names Open Security Alliance, 501(c)(3). The founder and runway statements appear only in the proposal and were not found elsewhere.
